tools.name: Evernote
tools.desc: Organize notes, photos, and documents in one place
pros: Ready to use out of the box, no local install or maintenance
Free tier available, try before you upgrade
cons: Advanced features and higher limits usually require a paid plan
usage:
Step: Open the official site and sign up
Click the red "Visit official site" button to open the Evernote homepage. Find "Sign Up" and log in with email or Google/GitHub.
Tip:
If the site won’t load, check your connection or try another browser.

Step: Pick the plan that fits you
New users usually get a free trial or free quota. Start with the Free tier before upgrading.
Check:
After sign-up you should see the Dashboard home.

Step: Create your first task / project
Click "New" or "Create New" and follow the guide. Pick the first template to start.
Tip:
Don’t start with a complex request. Test with one simple sentence, e.g. "Summarize this page into 3 points".

Step: Review and save the result
When done, the tool shows the result. Export, copy the link, or save locally.
Check:
If unhappy, click "Regenerate" or tweak the prompt and try again.
tools.detail: Evernote is a versatile productivity tool designed to help users organize notes, photos, and documents in one place. It allows users to create and store text notes, images, audio recordings, and even scanned documents. Key features include a powerful search function that can recognize text within images, the ability to sync notes across multiple devices, and a vast library of templates for different types of projects. Evernote is ideal for individuals, students, and professionals who need to manage a large volume of information and collaborate with others. Pros include its robust note-taking capabilities, seamless integration with other apps, and a user-friendly interface. Limitations may include a learning curve for some users and the need for a premium subscription for certain advanced features.

tools.detail: Microsoft OneNote is a digital note-taking application that enables users to capture, organize, and share their notes efficiently. It offers a wide range of tools for creating and formatting notes, including text, images, and tables. OneNote is particularly well-suited for students and professionals who need to manage complex projects and ideas. Key features include the ability to create notebooks with multiple sections, search for text within handwritten notes, and access notes from any device. OneNote is deeply integrated with the Microsoft ecosystem, allowing for easy sharing and collaboration with other Office 365 users. Pros include its robust note-taking features, strong integration with Microsoft products, and the ability to work offline. Limitations may include a less intuitive interface for some users and a reliance on the Microsoft ecosystem.

tools.detail: Trello is a visual collaboration tool that helps users organize tasks and projects in a visually appealing and intuitive way. It uses a card-based system to manage tasks, allowing users to create boards, lists, and cards to represent different stages of a project. Trello is particularly well-suited for teams working on projects with multiple steps and deadlines. Key features include the ability to assign tasks to team members, set due dates, and add comments and attachments to cards. Trello integrates with a wide range of other apps and services, making it a versatile tool for project management. Pros include its ease of use, visual approach to project management, and strong collaboration features. Limitations may include a lack of advanced project management features for complex projects and the potential for the interface to become cluttered with many cards and lists.

It allows users to create and connect notes in a non-linear manner, forming a network of ideas. Roam is particularly well-suited for researchers, writers, and anyone who needs to explore and connect concepts in a flexible and dynamic way. Key features include the ability to create links between notes, the use of blocks for different types of content, and the option to view notes in a graph view to see connections. Roam is known for its powerful search capabilities and the ability to export notes in various formats. Pros include its innovative approach to note-taking, strong search and organization features, and the potential for deep and meaningful connections between ideas. tools.detail: Google Docs Notes is a feature within the Google Docs platform that allows users to take notes directly within their documents. It is particularly useful for students, researchers, and professionals who need to annotate or add additional information to their Google Docs files. Users can create notes by clicking on the 'Add Note' button within the document, which opens a sidebar where they can type their notes. These notes are then visible to anyone with edit access to the document. Key features include the ability to format text within notes, add images, and link to other documents. Google Docs Notes is designed for users who are already familiar with the Google Docs interface and want a convenient way to add additional context or comments to their documents. Pros include its integration with the Google Drive ecosystem, real-time collaboration capabilities, and accessibility from any device with internet access. However, limitations include the fact that notes are not easily searchable within the document itself and the lack of a dedicated note-taking interface, which may be a drawback for users who prefer a more traditional note-taking experience.
